title: Integrator first-contact cheat journal
content:
Purpose and audience

This is a compact working journal for integrators (internal SEs + external platform partners) who are running first-contact sessions with new customers or internal teams evaluating Redwood’s client tooling. The goal: get a usable demo + a minimal production harness in under 90 minutes, capture the quick wins and the open questions, and leave a reproducible next step for the engineering team.

Tone: conversational / checklist-forward. Not a final playbook — this is the live notebook we take into calls and sync back to product/engine afterward.

Session template (60–90 minutes)

1) 0–5m: Quick alignment
- Intro + scope: what success looks like for this call (demo-only vs. integration pilot)
- Confirm constraints: private deployment? VPC? data residency? dedicated capacity?
- Primary persona: front-end dev, backend infra, or ML engineer?

2) 5–20m: Rapid capability check (tech discovery)
- Authentication method preference: API key / service principal / OIDC?
- Networking: can they reach our hosted endpoints? Any firewall/nat egress blocks?
- Models needed: chat/generation vs embeddings vs reranking? Latency SLO expectations?
- Runtime constraints: token budget, concurrency, and peak QPS patterns

3) 20–45m: Zero-to-demo path (pick one)
- Minimal demo (hosted API): sample curl and minimal app wiring
  - curl example: 
    curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
      -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \ 
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
      -d '{"model":"redwood-lite-1","input":"Summarize the following..."}'
- Local dev loop (sidecar / devkit): run starter container and swap API key
- Private deployment smoke (VPC): confirm control plane connectivity and list required firewall rules (443 outbound to control-plane.redwood.internal)

4) 45–70m: Instrumentation + guardrails
- Telemetry probes we add in the call:
  - token usage per request (client side)
  - request id propagation (X-Req-ID header)
  - latency histogram (p50/p95) and error counters
- Quick alert thresholds to propose: error-rate > 1% sustained, p95 latency above SLA by 30%
- Feature flags to keep: model-fallback, token-throttle, plan-based-rate-limit

5) 70–90m: Next steps & handoff
- Produce a tiny checklist for SRE and app eng
- Agree on pilot acceptance criteria (sample size, regression targets)
- Schedule a 1-week follow-up to review telemetry and prompt quality

Minimal artifacts produced during a session
- README.md (one-paragraph, repo root) with: how to run, where to swap keys, and what to verify
- smoke.sh or smoke.ps1 (curl-based) that runs 3 canonical calls (short chat, embeddings lookup, and small-batch generation)
- probes.md listing the telemetry events + required logs
- runbook fragment: what to do on 401/429/5xx

Rapid-templated checks (use during call)
- Authentication check: client can do curl with a test key and get 200 within 3 tries
- Latency sanity: first request < 700ms for small prompts (hosted)
- Embeddings sanity: cosine similarity between two similar strings > 0.85 (quick manual check)
- Fallthrough test: intentionally request an unavailable model and verify fallback path triggers (if configured)

Common friction patterns and quick mitigations
- No egress from customer environment: propose a temporary reverse-proxy flow or provide a local-stubbed devkit image (see linked PR)
- Keys leaked into logs: remind to redact and add token rotation step to runbook
- Prompt drift: capture 20 failed examples and flag for prompt tuning / few-shot examples
- Unexpected cost: enable per-route quotas and demo enabling the cost dashboard in Console

Starter checklist for a follow-up pilot repo (to seed during call)
- /README.md: 5 bullets (how to run, config examples, expected outputs)
- /smoke.sh: 3 canonical requests + exit codes
- /telemetry/README.md: which metrics to collect and where they flow (console + prometheus scrape)
- /prompts/canonical-10.txt: set of 10 baseline prompts for quality regression tests
- /rollout/notes.md: desired canary % and rollback criteria

Unresolved questions to capture during first contact (capture verbatim)
- "We need FIPS 140 KMS integration—what's the timeline?"
- "Can we pin to a quantized variant of the model to reduce cost for embeddings?"
- "How do we enable VPC peering with our on-prem control plane?"

Post-call actions (owner + ETA)
- Create the pilot repo skeleton (owner: Marcus) — ETA: 48h
- Add telemetry hooks to example (owner: Elena) — ETA: 72h
- Open infra request for firewall rule (owner: customer infra lead, CC: Devon) — ETA: 3 business days
- Hand to solutions-eng for SLA procurement if Dedicated needed (owner: Sofia) — ETA: 5 business days

Notes to self (informal jots)
- When the customer says "low-latency", ask if they mean p50 or p95 — different solutions (batching vs. routing)
- Keep the curl examples tiny; engineers will copy/paste into their terminals — avoid multi-line JSON pain by providing minimal examples and a script
- For private deployments, bring up the audit-log retention plan early — legal often asks at procurement time

Snippets to paste in a call (copy-ready)
- Quick sample config for devkit env.yaml:
  REDWOOD_KEY: "<paste-key-here>"
  REDWOOD_ENDPOINT: "https://api.redwood.ai/v1"
- smoke.sh starter:
  #!/usr/bin/env bash
  set -euo pipefail
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-lite-1","input":"hello"}' $REDWOOD_ENDPOINT/generate | jq '.'

Where to sync after the call
- Drop the repo link and a 1-paragraph summary into the Confluence page (DEVEXP-453) and tag the ticket (ENG-789).
- Add a short note to #integrations Slack (channel) with the headline and next step owner.

Appendix: quick decision heuristics
- If customer requires private deployment + < 50ms p95, propose Dedicated GPU + local KV cache.
- If data residency + no egress, put them on the Private (on-prem) path — escalate to sales for licensing.
- If early-stage startup with cost sensitivity, propose hosted + aggressive batching + 8-bit quantized model recommendations.

End log — keep this file lean and copy forward into specific customer docs.

Last updated by: Sofia Patel (notes from 2026-03-10 session with ACME Retail)
